title: The Well That Learned to Say No
blurb: The bucket's education, dated. Before December 2020 an overwrite in S3 could be followed by a read of the old copy; then reads became the latest, always. A race with the condition pulled out shows why fresh reads are not enough: an overwrite can win the well, but it cannot take back what was already served. In August 2024 the well learns to refuse a second creation; in November 2024 to refuse a stale replacement: compare and swap. Then the reversal: who referees the referee? Werner Vogels's witness inside S3, proved before it was trusted. celld's warning that a store can look compatible and silently ignore the condition, and the four test writes every node makes before it serves. And the scope: one key, one plate, no promise that two rooms commit as one.

lines.text: Back to the square. In our harbour the Well stands for a bucket in an object store, like Amazon's S3.
lines.direction: re-establishing, unhurried; 'S3' said 'ess three'

lines.text: There was a time when overwriting a file in S3 and reading it straight back could hand you the old copy.
lines.direction: a small historical oddity, told plainly

lines.text: Amazon later explained why: a write could take one path through its caches, and a read another.
lines.direction: explanatory, the two paths separated in the voice

lines.text: On the first of December, 2020, that changed: read after a write, and you get the latest.
lines.direction: a date with weight; 'the latest' placed

lines.text: Whatever bucket you draw up is the newest.
lines.direction: the metaphor stated once, quietly satisfied

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the Well's first lesson, freshness. Iris open on the Room Lantern's reflection in the Well's water (the chapter's motivated light), then pull up and out to the canonical square: the Well at the left third, the Plate on its iron frame above it, House A's lit window up on the L3 terrace, the L6 lamp-post at frame right. A brass badge 'Amazon S3' hangs on a hook at the wellhead from the first frame (the store's own behaviour; unnamed beyond the line). Camera: a slow truck left over 6 s with a slight dolly in toward the wellhead. On 'old copy' the keeper of House A, at the wellhead, lowers a scroll marked with a fresh ink stroke into the Well, then draws the bucket straight back up: the scroll in it carries the PREVIOUS, faded stroke (beat stale). On 'path' a cutaway sliver opens down the well shaft (a narrow vertical section, serverCyan glints, foreshadowing s04): the lowered scroll descends a left-hand channel while the drawn-up bucket rises through a right-hand channel that the new scroll has not reached (beat paths); the sliver closes. On 'December' a date stamp sets (beat date). On 'latest' the action repeats: down goes the fresh stroke, up comes the same fresh stroke, and a small brass ring on the bucket's handle catches the moonlight (beat fresh). On 'newest' the camera settles on the full bucket held at the wellhead lip; the water below steadies (beat newest). Label upper-left only; nothing below y 634.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: PULL THE PIN, the naive race (first use of the film's pin device). Lamp change in from s01 to the emberRed failure grade as the demonstrator's hand arrives (failures enter by lampChange). Framing: the wellhead centre-left, the Plate above it, its three brass tiles BLANK; Houses A (screen-left) and B (screen-right) on the L3 terrace, both windows dark. At the wellhead the Tooth: a brass slot with a small shutter and, seated in its pawl, a red-tagged brass pin. On 'pin' the demonstrator's hand enters from lower RIGHT, pinches the red tag and draws the pin out; the Tooth's pawl drops slack (beat pull). On 'nobody' both keepers, arriving from either side, glance up at the blank Plate at the same moment (beat read); on 'mine' each slides a brass swap card into the now-unguarded slot and each card's house letter is stamped onto the first tile in turn: first 'A', then, overwriting it, 'B' a beat later (beat write). On 'lanterns' BOTH windows light, a Room Lantern in each, two copies of the harbour room (beat both); small message slips start drifting into both lanterns. On 'later' the Plate's first tile settles on 'B' (beat wins). On 'answered' a slip leaves A's lantern with a tick: A's room has already promised something (beat served). On 'overwrite' the camera pushes in on the Plate reading B while A's lantern still glows beside it (beat maxim). On 'moved' a quick ink-line diagram draws upper-left over the sky: 'read … write' with a gap between them in which a second hand slips its card (beat gap). On 'Pin back' the hand reseats the red pin; the pawl snaps tight; the grade lamp-changes back toward winterBlue as both lanterns gutter out (beat reseat). Text upper-left only; nothing below y 634.

lines.text: The twentieth of August, 2024. S3 learns its first refusal: write this only if nothing is there.
lines.direction: a date, then the rule in plain words, as if reading a new sign at the well

lines.text: Two keepers race. One creation lands, a shutter drops, and the second card is refused.
lines.direction: mechanical and satisfying; 'refused' with a small click in it

lines.text: The twenty-fifth of November, 2024: replace this only if it is still the version I read.
lines.direction: the same cadence as L0313, a rhyme across three months

lines.text: Both cards carry the same old version. One click: accepted, and the Plate's notch is cut anew. One thunk: refused.
lines.direction: two sounds in words; 'click' light, 'thunk' low

lines.text: That is compare and swap, and the store checks the condition, not the keeper.
lines.direction: naming the trade term; 'the store' stressed

lines.text: The Well had learned to say no.
lines.direction: a short list landing on the chapter title; warm

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the two refusals that make the Well a referee, one machine, two lessons. Cut on the pin's click into a tight two-shot of the wellhead (camera low, the Plate looming above). Badge 'Amazon S3' still on its hook. LESSON ONE on 'August' (date stamp, beat date1): the Plate's tiles are blank; the Tooth's slot is OPEN with a small hinged shutter above it. On 'race' keepers A and B (hands and forearms only, from left and right) push swap cards toward the slot at the same moment (beat race); on 'lands' A's card goes in first, the tile stamps 'A' (illustrative), and on 'shutter' the shutter drops with a dry click over the slot (beat shutter); on 'refused' B's card strikes the closed shutter and is spat back, punched with a small hole (beat refuse1). LESSON TWO on 'November' (second date stamp replaces the first, beat date2): the Plate now shows a notched brass edge, a little sawtooth profile that stands for its current version (an opaque mark, NOT a checksum; shown as a pattern only). On 'carry' both keepers hold up cards whose edges carry the SAME sawtooth: each read the same version (beat notch). On 'click' A's card meets the edge, the profiles mesh, the tile turns to the next claim and the Plate's notch is visibly re-cut into a new pattern (beat click); on 'thunk' B's card, still carrying the old pattern, fails to mesh and is spat back punched (beat thunk). On 'compare' the term tag paints (beat term). On 'store' the camera tilts down past the wellhead to the Well's mouth: the check happens down there, inside the store, not in either keeper's hand (beat store). On 'no' pull back to the square, the Plate gleaming above the Well (beat no). Text upper-left; bottom 12% clear.

shots.setting: inside the Well (a metaphorical cutaway of an object store): a vertical section of stone cisterns and ledges lit by serverCyan glints, a small lamp-keeper with a bell on a ledge, an order ledger; at the top, beside the shaft, a lectern-height desk where Werner Vogels stands

lines.text: So who referees the referee?
lines.direction: the film's first reversal; a genuine question, then let it hang

lines.text: In April 2021, Werner Vogels, Amazon's chief technology officer, described what they had built inside S3.
lines.direction: an attribution, respectful and plain

lines.text: Caches that agree with one another, an order for every object's changes, and a witness, told of every change, that any cache can ask: is my copy stale?
lines.direction: three parts, a beat between each; 'witness' lifted slightly

lines.text: They checked it with proofs and model checking, which, he wrote, was more work than building it.
lines.direction: admiring, a touch wry at the end

lines.text: So the houses on the hill run no consensus of their own. The coordination has moved inside the Well.
lines.direction: the chapter's thesis; slow; 'moved inside the Well' landed low

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: WHO REFEREES THE REFEREE? A vertical crane down into the Well. Cut from the square to a tight top-down of the wellhead; on 'referee' the camera cranes down the shaft (about 6 s, cubic) as the stone wall dissolves into a cutaway section (the style bible's 'cutaway' register, serverCyan glints only here): L2 stone cisterns stacked in depth, L3 narrow ledges, fog sheet A between them. At the top of the shaft, beside the cutaway, a standing silhouette at a lectern-height desk: Werner Vogels, generic and dignified, no likeness; name card on 'Vogels' (beat name). On 'agree' three small cistern-lamps at different depths brighten together, the same faint mark reflected in each (beat caches). On 'order' a narrow paper ledger on a ledge advances one line per change, in sequence (beat order). On 'witness' the witness appears: a small lamp-keeper on a mid-ledge with a hand-bell; a scroll drops past him from above and he rings once; at the same moment a cistern-lamp below, about to hand up an old copy, tugs a cord up to the witness, sees the bell's flag raised, and its old copy dims while the fresh one is fetched (beat witness: the read barrier, shown as a cord and a flag). On 'proofs' a sheaf of parchment proof-sheets is pinned along the shaft wall beside the ledges, more sheets than the ledges themselves (beat proofs; this is the image of 'more work than building it'). On 'hill' the camera cranes back UP the shaft (4 s, cubic) to the square: the three houses above, each keeper's pulley line converging on the one wellhead; inside the Well a faint cyan pulse shows the machinery still turning (beat inside). Quotes upper-left on a soft plate, one replacing the other; bottom 12% clear.

lines.text: Now a warning, from celld's own documentation.
lines.direction: a new voice in the story, introduced matter-of-factly; the version spoken as numbers

lines.text: Some stores speak S3's language but do not keep these conditions; on them, two houses can own one room.
lines.direction: serious, not alarmist

lines.text: Worse, a store can accept the condition and silently ignore it.
lines.direction: lower; the danger is in the silence

lines.text: So before it serves, every celld node makes four test writes: create, refuse a second create, update, refuse a stale update. Two must fail.
lines.direction: a checklist read briskly; 'must fail' with relish

lines.text: Then it checks a ranged read. No node can skip the test.
lines.direction: two short facts

lines.text: A bucket earns its place by refusing, on demand.
lines.direction: an aphorism, smiling

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: 'compatible' is not a guarantee. Occluder wipe behind the L6 lamp-post: the square now holds TWO wells side by side, identical in stone, rope and bucket; the right-hand one's Tooth is bright and unworn. A labGreen work-lamp hangs over the right well; a brass badge 'celld 0.6.3' hangs on a small test rig beside it (the rig, not the well, carries the badge). On 'documentation' a quote card starts upper-left (beat doc). On 'room' the familiar race replays at the right well in miniature: two swap cards go in and BOTH are accepted; two tiny lanterns light on the terrace (beat two). On 'ignore' a close-up: the right well's shutter swings shut over the slot as if refusing, yet the second card slides in underneath it anyway, without a sound (beat silent). On 'test' the test rig: four brass cards on a rack, labelled by small engraved symbols for create, create again, update, stale update; the rig feeds them one at a time into the LEFT well: accept, REFUSE (spat back), accept, REFUSE (beat four), and two small green check lamps light over the two refusals (beat twofail on 'fail'). On 'ranged' a brass measuring rod is lowered into the left well and draws up exactly the marked span of a scroll (beat range). On 'skip' the rig's lid locks shut with a padlock silhouette (beat lock). On 'refusing' the camera settles on the left well; the right well darkens and recedes into fog (beat earn). Text upper-left; bottom 12% clear.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the scope of the referee. Cut to a high angle over the terrace looking down on the square. The iron frame above the Well now carries TWO plates side by side: the harbour room's Plate and a second, smaller plate for an illustrative second room whose lantern glows in House B. On 'key' a thin brass line ties each plate to its own slot in the Tooth; the camera eases in (beat keys). On 'two' the two rooms each try to change at once: a slip enters each lantern; one plate's card clicks, the other's is still in flight; the two slips are visibly NOT tied together, and no cord joins the two plates (beat apart). On 'quiet' the Well's water darkens, the rope goes slack, and every keeper's card hangs unanswered at the slot; the plates stay frozen (beat quiet). Hold; then iris out, closing on the harbour room's lantern (the chapter's end). Label upper-left; bottom 12% clear.
